analysis.name: Loaded Oatmeal Breakfast with Coffee

items.name: Oatmeal with banana, peanut butter, blueberries and honey
items.portion: 1 cup dry rolled oats cooked in water, 1 medium banana, 2 tbsp peanut butter, ~1/2 cup blueberries, 1 tbsp honey

analysis.notes: Oatmeal and its stir-ins logged as one dish; coffee logged separately as the drink. Portions assumed: 1 cup dry oats (~80 g), medium banana, heaping tablespoon of peanut butter treated as ~2 tbsp (32 g), handful of blueberries ~75 g, honey drizzle ~1 tbsp. Solid pre-run carb load (~117 g carbs).

analysis.name: Post-Workout Recovery Shake

items.name: Vanilla whey recovery shake (whey, oat milk, frozen banana, almond butter)
items.portion: 1 large blended shake (~16 oz): 1 scoop whey, 1 cup oat milk, 1 medium-large frozen banana, 1 heaping tbsp almond butter

analysis.notes: Logged as one blended drink since all components go into a single shake. Your 400 kcal guess is close but slightly low — a full scoop of whey (~120 kcal), 1 cup oat milk (~120 kcal), a medium-large banana (~110 kcal) and a heaping spoon of almond butter (~100 kcal) land nearer 450–470 kcal. Carb:protein ratio (~1.6:1) is solid for glycogen resynthesis and muscle repair after endurance work. Exact numbers depend on your whey brand and whether the oat milk is sweetened/barista style (barista versions can add 30–50 kcal and more fat).

analysis.name: Pre-Ride Carb Breakfast: Toast with Jam & Honey, Banana, Coffee

items.portion: 2 slices with ~1.5 tbsp jam and ~1 tbsp honey

items.name: Coffee with a splash of milk
items.portion: 12 oz brewed coffee with ~2 tbsp whole milk

analysis.notes: Portions inferred from typical athlete servings: 2 standard white bread slices, a large banana, and a modest milk splash. Butter was not mentioned so none was included. Very carb-dense and low in fat/fiber, which fits a pre-long-ride strategy; consider adding on-bike carbs since protein here is low.

Sodium is high, typical of restaurant bowls — good for post-training electrolyte replacement.
